The Night Before You Sail

Pre-Cruise Stay in Seattle

◆ ◆ ◆
Since you're flying in on June 12, the day before your cruise, we've got you settled at Staypineapple Hotel FIVE in Belltown — a quick, easy taxi from Sea-Tac airport and walking distance to Pike Place Market, the Space Needle, and the cruise terminal at Pier 91 (about 10 minutes by car).

A charming boutique hotel known for its quirky, welcoming personality — pineapple cupcakes at check-in, robes you'll actually want to use, and beds known across the chain as some of the most comfortable in Seattle. Right in the heart of downtown with the Space Needle three blocks away.

From Your Travel Advisor On embarkation morning, ask the front desk to call you a taxi or rideshare to Pier 91 (the Smith Cove Cruise Terminal) — that's where Royal Princess is docked. Aim to arrive at the pier between 11:30 AM and 1:00 PM for the smoothest check-in. Princess boarding usually starts around 12:30 PM, and the ship sails at 3:00 PM sharp.
Your Ship

The Royal Princess

A grand Royal-class flagship — refined, spacious, and built to soak in the Inside Passage from every angle.

◆ ◆ ◆
Princess Cruises · Royal-Class
Royal Princess
Christened by Catherine, Duchess of Cambridge · Sailing since 2013 · Refurbished 2019

Here's a quick tour of what's onboard. Everything in this section is included in your fare — pools, theater, dining, deck space, and more.
The Piazza
A three-deck marble atrium at the ship's heart — the natural gathering spot for coffee, cocktails, and live music throughout the day.
Princess Theater
A two-story West End-style theater with Broadway-caliber productions, nightly. No reservation needed — just show up.
Pool Deck & Movies Under the Stars
Four pools, nine hot tubs, and a giant outdoor LED screen for nightly movies poolside — popcorn and blankets included.
Your Balcony Stateroom
A private balcony is the right call for Alaska — coffee in the morning with glaciers drifting past your door. Twin beds as requested.
SeaWalk & Top-Deck Promenade
A glass-floored walkway that extends 28 feet over the side of the ship — and a full wraparound promenade for sunset strolls.
Six Included Dining Venues
Three main dining rooms, the Horizon Court buffet, the International Café, and the pizza-and-grill at the pool — all included.
A Few Things Worth Knowing Your dining is set to Maître d' style (flexible — show up when you like). Drinks, specialty restaurants, the spa, and shore excursions are extra. We can add a Princess Plus or Premier package if you'd like beverages and Wi-Fi bundled in — just say the word.

Shore Excursions

Easy, Low-Key Picks for Each Port

◆ ◆ ◆
Here are gentle, mostly-seated excursion ideas for each port — boats, motor coaches, and walkable cultural stops. Tap any option that catches your eye and we'll follow up to book it (either through Princess directly for the convenience, or independently for a better price).
Juneau · Monday, June 15
1:00 PM – 9:15 PM · 8 hours ashore
Whales & the Mendenhall Glacier
Juneau Wildlife Whale Watching & Mendenhall Glacier
The classic Juneau combo. Sheltered catamaran for whale watching, then a stop at the Mendenhall Glacier visitor center. Boat ramps and an easy paved path at the glacier.
★ 4.96,270 reviews4.5 hrs · seated boat tourFree cancellation
Starting from$249per person
Ultimate Juneau Whale Watch & Mendenhall Glacier View
Same idea, shorter (3 hrs) and a better value — the glacier is a photo stop rather than a long visit. Great if you'd rather have more free time downtown afterward.
★ 4.87926 reviews3 hrs · seated boat tourFree cancellation
Starting from$156per person
On-Your-Own · Mt. Roberts Tramway + Tracy's King Crab Shack
The tram leaves right from the pier — six minutes up to a viewing platform 1,800 feet above the city. Back down, Tracy's King Crab Shack is a five-minute walk for legendary crab bisque.
~$45/pp tramway · meals separateSelf-guided · all paved & easy
Estimated$45tram only
Skagway · Tuesday, June 16
6:00 AM – 8:15 PM · 14 hours ashore
Gold Rush history & White Pass
Skagway City & White Pass Summit Tour
A relaxed motor coach tour — historic downtown narration, then up the spectacular White Pass scenic highway with photo stops at every viewpoint. The easiest way to see the famous scenery without a long train ride.
★ 4.88417 reviews2.5 hrs · seated coachFree cancellation
Starting from$76per person
White Pass Deluxe Tour
All summit, no town. Three hours along the historic White Pass route with rest stops and viewpoint pull-offs. A great value pick if the city center isn't on your list.
★ 4.68437 reviews3 hrs · seated coachFree cancellation
Starting from$70per person
On-Your-Own · Historic Downtown Walk
Seven walkable blocks of preserved 1898 gold rush buildings, museums, candy shops, and the National Park Visitor Center (free, with a fascinating film). Benches everywhere — no rush.
FreeSelf-guided · flat & walkable
Starting fromFree
Glacier Bay National Park · Wednesday, June 17
6:00 AM – 2:30 PM · Scenic cruising · No port stop
The signature day

No excursion needed — this day is the excursion. Royal Princess sails deep into Glacier Bay National Park, where a National Park Service ranger boards the ship to narrate. You'll get within a mile of glaciers, watch them calve, and likely spot whales, seals, sea otters, and bald eagles — all from your balcony or the top deck. Bring binoculars, hot coffee, and a warm layer. This is what people remember most about Alaska.

Ketchikan · Thursday, June 18
7:00 AM – 1:15 PM · 6 hours ashore
Totem poles & the famous Lumberjack Show
Alaskan Cultural, Culinary & Lumberjack Show Experience
A relaxed three-and-a-half-hour package — city sightseeing, a tasting of local Alaskan foods, and front-row seats at the Great Alaskan Lumberjack Show (it's a hoot). Fits well inside the port window.
★ 4.74230 reviews3 hrs 45 minFree cancellation
Starting from$149per person
Saxman Native Village, City Highlights & Lumberjack Show
Tlingit cultural visit at Saxman with the world's largest collection of standing totem poles, a quick highlights tour, then the Lumberjack Show. Mostly motor coach with short, easy walks.
★ 4.4102 reviews4 hrs 25 minFree cancellation
Starting from$129per person
On-Your-Own · Creek Street + Lumberjack Show
Creek Street's wooden boardwalk is right next to the pier — flat and photogenic, with galleries and the Dolly's House Museum. The Lumberjack Show venue is a 5-minute walk. Tickets at the door.
~$45/pp show onlySelf-guided · paved & boardwalk
Estimated$45show only
Victoria, BC · Friday, June 19
9:00 PM – 11:59 PM · 3 hours ashore (after dark)
A late-night ceremonial stop

Our honest recommendation: enjoy this one from the ship. The late arrival means most attractions are closed, the shuttle ride into town eats nearly an hour each way, and you'll want to be aboard for the late-night sail back to Seattle. From the deck or your balcony, you'll have a beautiful view of the Parliament Buildings and Empress Hotel lit up across the Inner Harbour — a perfect last-night nightcap. If you'd like a quick stroll, the Ogden Point breakwater pier is a flat walk right from the cruise terminal.
